# PDF Tool, Site Quality, and AdSense Readiness Checklist

This is the persistent evidence log. Update the observed result and evidence when a check is run. A build or visible control alone does not verify a user flow. AdSense readiness is not approval.

**PDF ↔ Markdown selected-file actions align to the card edge (2026-11-04):** Applied a scoped auto left margin to the Replace/Remove group in both selected-file directions, keeping the actions after the filename and at the far end of each attachment card. The regression failed before implementation and passes afterward; `node --test tests/markdownToolRoute.test.mjs` passes 6/6. The build succeeds with the existing warnings and `git diff --check` passes. Visual browser alignment was not confirmed. **IMPLEMENTED — NOT YET VERIFIED**

Chromium measured 52px heights on all four conversion actions and 14px Markdown label text at desktop width. Mobile cross-tool comparison was not verified. **PARTIALLY VERIFIED**

## Status key

- **PASS — VERIFIED**: executed; expected result observed.
- **PARTIALLY VERIFIED**: representative behavior passed; remaining checks are stated.
- **PASS — ALREADY PRESENT**: existing behavior inspected and verified.
- **IMPLEMENTED — NOT YET VERIFIED**: code exists, but behavior is not fully tested.
- **NEEDS USER ACTION**: owner, publisher ID, live domain, account, consent decision, or legal review needed.
- **BLOCKED**: a concrete environment/tooling constraint prevents the check.
- **FAIL**: executed check did not meet its expected result.

**Preview-use guidance consistency (2026-11-02):** Applied the shared 16 px semibold, blue-left-accent callout to interactive preview guidance across nine PDF/image workflows, including page selection, crop bounds, editing, reordering, and redaction. Regression coverage confirms the shared CSS treatment and that each workflow uses it. Full suite passes 187/187; production build succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Browser visual verification was not performed.

**Merge settings placement (2026-11-02):** Moved output filename, page size, source bookmarks, and blank-page controls between the merge-mode buttons and the conditional page-selection workspace. An order regression test failed before the change and passes afterward; focused Merge tests pass 9/9, the full suite passes 181/181, the production build succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. Browser visual verification of the new order was not performed.

**Encrypted-PDF rejection notification (2026-11-01):** Replaced the misleading “password-protected PDF” error with a shared message explaining that encryption or security restrictions may prevent processing even when the file opens without a password. Both ordinary PDF validation and Merge output validation use the shared text; file rejection is unchanged. Focused merge/notification tests pass 6/6, the full suite passes 169/169, the production build succeeds with existing warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. A real encrypted-with-empty-password fixture was not tested.

English point copy is specific to each tool; point headings are translated for supported locales, and other localized copy reuses the existing localized tool descriptions and workflow guidance. Removed redundant “unencrypted” wording from descriptions and steps while preserving relevant PDF password restrictions in attachment guidance; image input and the unavailable Excel page do not show that restriction. Browser checks confirmed the three-point display on Merge desktop and PDF ↔ Markdown mobile, with no horizontal document overflow; light-theme and remaining-page visual review are still outstanding.

At 1280 px the desktop panel icon and existing position remain unchanged. `npm.cmd test` passes 98 tests; the production build succeeds with the existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes.

**Tool-page Back button removal (2026-11-01):** Removed the visible Back control and its responsive/theme styling. The attachment-aware discard dialog and navigation guard remain for tool search, in-app links, browser history, and reload/close warnings. Chromium confirmed zero Back-button elements on Edit PDF. `npm.cmd test` passes 97 tests; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes.

**Tool-page Back destination and placement (2026-11-01):** Back now always goes to Home, regardless of which page opened the tool, and is positioned inside the upper-left of the shared tool hero card. Chromium verified the button is contained in the hero, that direct entry to `/sign` followed by Back reaches `/`, and that with a valid PDF attached the dialog fits at 320 px, cancel retains the file/route, and confirmation goes Home. Existing regression tests cover attachment tracking for every file-based tool, localized dialog text, and history interception. `npm.cmd test` passes 98 tests, `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. Native reload/tab-close prompts, screen-reader behavior, and other browsers remain unverified.

**Split PDF mobile layout (2026-11-01):** With a generated 12-page PDF split into 12 output files, browser checks at 320 px showed a 305 px document width; the selected-file card and action buttons, result panel, output card, and download button all stayed within their parents. The mode controls wrap, the attachment shell reports visible overflow for the glow, and generated-file names/download controls have readable theme-aware colors. Added four responsive regression tests; `npm.cmd test` passes 88 tests, `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. Actual save-to-disk behavior and assistive-technology/cross-browser behavior were not retested.

**Mobile collapse control placement (2026-11-01):** Earlier iteration (superseded by the centered edge handle above) reused the existing sidebar collapse button and kept it out of the top search/utility area. At 390 px, collapsing expanded workspace/search width from 275.2 px to 351.2 px, and the document width stayed 375 px. Desktop placement remained unchanged. At that stage `npm.cmd test` passed 90 tests and the production build succeeded with the existing warnings.

**Extra-narrow mobile attachment actions (2026-11-01):** The shared Replace/Remove icon actions wrap below 380 px. Browser verification with a valid local PDF showed two separate 36×36 px rows at 320 px and one 76×36 px row at 390 px; both layouts fit within the selected-file card with no horizontal document overflow. `npm.cmd test` passes 89 tests, `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. Only Split PDF was exercised in the browser; other tools using the shared controls and assistive-technology behavior were not retested.

**Search and fixed utilities do not overlap (2026-11-01):** Removed viewport-based inline sizing and reserved space in the topbar for the fixed Privacy/Contact/About/theme controls rendered by `.site-left-bottom`. The first pass incorrectly assumed these controls were hidden at 580 px and narrower; the corrected narrow breakpoint retains the 10.5rem right reservation. A regression test failed before the CSS fix and passed afterward. Chromium measured an 11.2 px gap with expanded search at 320, 398, 462, 494, 580, 581, and 900 px; at 901 px the gap was 54.2 px and at 1280 px it was 164 px. At 320 px the search control remains 48 px wide to avoid covering utility buttons. `npm.cmd test` passes 99/99; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with the existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Deployed behavior and other browsers remain unverified.

**Mobile search suggestions (2026-10-31):** Expanded the mobile results panel independently of the search input. Browser measurements at 390 px show a 270.4 px panel; at 320 px it is 200 px, remains inside the viewport, and the document width is 305 px. `npm.cmd test` passes 84 tests, `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with the existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. This updates the mobile search behavior in the Header/footer navigation check; deployed and assistive-technology behavior were not retested.

**Lazy-route review follow-up (2026-10-31):** Route focus now waits for the destination heading after lazy content loads. A localized error boundary handles rejected route chunks, recovers on navigation, and offers a reload action. The local production preview confirmed focus after navigation to Merge, the fallback when the Split chunk was deliberately blocked, and successful navigation to FAQ from the error state. `npm.cmd test` passes 83 tests, `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with the existing `buffer` externalization/large-chunk warnings, `npm.cmd audit` reports zero advisories, and `git diff --check` passes. This does not verify Netlify-hosted headers/redirects, downloads to disk, screen readers, other browsers, or AdSense readiness.

**Netlify pre-deployment audit (2026-10-31):** Added `public/_redirects` for SPA route fallback, `public/_headers` with `nosniff`, strict-origin referrer policy, frame denial, and camera/microphone/geolocation restrictions, plus `.nvmrc` for Node `24.22.0`. Added a scoped `npm test` script and route-code-splitting/deployment tests; all 79 checked-in tests pass. Production build passes and the main app chunk fell from 2.20 MB to 798.57 KB (274.76 KB gzip); the >500 KB chunk warning remains. An isolated clean `npm ci`, the copied tests, and production build all passed. Full and production-only npm audits report zero advisories. A source import audit found no case-sensitive import failures. Production-preview checks covered 38 routes at desktop and 390 px widths; all rendered without page errors, failed requests, or horizontal overflow. All 18 active PDF tools rejected a corrupt fixture without retaining it; valid fixtures were accepted, except Unlock correctly rejects an unencrypted PDF. Fresh-origin OCR fetched only same-origin worker/core/language assets and produced a searchable one-page PDF. Protect PDF output was confirmed AES-256 R6/256-bit, rejected an incorrect password, and decrypted with the correct password. Unlock PDF browser checks rejected a wrong password and generated an unencrypted, two-page PDF with the correct password. PDF-to-Word generated a valid DOCX ZIP whose document XML retained the two expected source strings. Compression retained an already-optimized 1.1 KB PDF without offering a larger download; Higher compression showed its quality-loss warning and reduced a synthetic image PDF from 18 KB to 5.5 KB (70.1%). These tool checks validate representative fixtures, not every file type, output fidelity, or actual browser-to-disk download. Netlify-served headers/fallback, screen readers, other browsers, Lighthouse, live hosting behavior, and owner/legal/AdSense prerequisites remain outstanding. No commit, push, or deployment was made.

**Remove PDF Pages selected-file follow-up (2026-10-30):** Separated the selected row from upload-zone styles and prevented expected stale PDF-preview cancellation from being reported as a render failure. On `/remove-pages`, a synthetic PDF showed aligned file details and filename-specific Replace/Remove actions; removing the file returned to the chooser. Desktop card geometry was 1079.2×73.6 px with no details/action overlap. At a 390 px viewport, the card was 241.6×133.6 px with no overlap and document width 375 px. Removing during a 24-page preview produced no console errors. Production build, targeted Problems checks, and `git diff --check` pass. The PDF removal output flow was not retested; the shared component change also applies to Extract PDF Pages.

**All-tool attachment border effect (2026-10-30):** Applied the expanded blue pulse (7 px ring and 32 px diffuse glow at peak) to all shared tool attachment sections, and disabled it for reduced-motion preferences. Browser verified the expected animation on all 18 active tool routes and `animation: none` on Merge with reduced motion enabled. `npm.cmd run build` and `git diff --check` pass. The Excel/PowerPoint limitation pages do not have attachment sections and remain unchanged.

**Shared selected-file cards (2026-10-30):** Reused the neutral Merge-style document tile and filename-specific Replace/Remove icon controls across all 18 active tool routes; Image to PDF retains its image previews. Browser file-selection sweeps confirmed matching tile colors on every route in both themes (light `rgb(241, 245, 249)` / `rgb(100, 116, 139)`; dark `rgb(30, 41, 59)` / `rgb(167, 179, 197)`), with action `title` tooltips, `aria-label`s, and decorative SVGs hidden from assistive technology. Invalid and valid replacement plus deletion were tested on Split PDF; replacement kept the same slot in Compress PDF and Image to PDF; invalid image replacement preserved the selected image, and cancelling the Image-to-PDF replacement picker showed no error. PDF processing/output flows were not retested. `npm.cmd run build` and `git diff --check` pass; existing bundle warnings remain.

**Merge per-file actions (2026-10-30):** Added Replace and Remove icon buttons on each Merge PDF file card. Browser verified each button exposes a filename-specific `aria-label` and `title`, invalid replacement preserves the existing file, valid replacement updates the same row, and deleting one or the last file removes it and restores focus appropriately. Automated browser interaction used two valid synthetic one-page PDFs and one invalid `.pdf`. `npm.cmd run build`, the Problems check, and `git diff --check` pass. Inline SVGs are correctly decorative/`aria-hidden`; button labels provide accessible names because SVG icons do not use `alt`.

**Protect & Extract attachment match (2026-10-30):** Protect PDF, Unlock PDF, Compress PDF, Split PDF, and OCR PDF now use the shared Merge upload-card structure; Extract PDF Pages already used it. At the browser's available 1355 px CSS viewport, Merge and each of the six routes measured 994×88 px. Each chooser opened a file picker; Compress correctly opened a multi-file picker and the other routes opened single-file pickers. Attachment rules preserve Unlock's password-protected input and OCR's 50-page limit; Split no longer displays an unverified 50-page cap. Mobile measurements could not be confirmed because the browser viewport remained 1355 px after resize requests. No PDF selection, processing, or output flow was retested. Build and diff checks pass.

**Attachment visual follow-up (2026-10-30):** Browser comparisons confirmed that Merge, Rotate, Remove Pages, Crop, Organize, and all four Edit & Sign tools share the attachment-card pattern. The Edit & Sign set matched Merge at 919×88 px on a 1280×900 viewport and 242×219 px at 390×844; document scroll width was 375 px. Their 40×40 px icon tiles, 16 px headings, 14 px subtitles, and 14 px/600-weight 40 px-high blue buttons match in light and dark themes. Each chooser invoked its file input, and each route accepted a synthetic one-page PDF and displayed its filename/page count. PDF creation workflows remain untested.

**Shared attachment top padding (2026-10-30):** Set `.tool-attachment-content` top padding to `1.25rem` (20px at the default 16px root size) across tool attachment sections; horizontal and bottom padding remain 1.25rem. The production build and `git diff --check` pass. Browser geometry was not measured.
